title: The Scientific Basis of Guideline Recommendations on Sugar Intake: A Systematic Review
authors: Erickson J, Sadeghirad B, Lytvyn L, Slavin J, Johnston BC
funder: This project was funded by the Technical Committee on Dietary Carbohydrates of ILSI North America. The authors wrote the protocol, the scope of which was reviewed and approved by ILSI; and conducted the study independently from ILSI. The abstract states that the funding source is primarily supported by the food and agriculture industry.
authorConflicts: J. Slavin received the ILSI North America grant for this project, research funds from food companies including PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, Danone and Nestlé Health Sciences, and serves on scientific advisory boards of Tate and Lyle, Kerry Ingredients, Atkins Nutritionals and Midwest Dairy Association; B.C. Johnston was a methods consultant to ILSI for this project.
result: 9 guidelines with 12 recommendations; each advised less consumption of foods containing nonintrinsic sugars. Guidelines scored poorly on AGREE II for rigour of development, applicability and editorial independence; 5 recommendations set limits from less than 25% to less than 5% of energy; quality of the supporting evidence was low to very low. The authors concluded that the guidelines do not meet criteria for trustworthy recommendations.
